items.question_text:
You are performing a monthly security check of your Google Cloud environment and want to know who has access to view data stored in your Google Cloud
Project. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Identity and Access Management (IAM) defines the current permissions and roles assigned to users and service accounts within a Google Cloud Project. Reviewing IAM policies reveals exactly who has the authorization to view data at the present moment.

In contrast, Audit Logs record historical activity of who accessed resources in the past, not necessarily who currently holds permission if they have not recently acted.

choices.text: Enable Audit Logs for all APIs that are related to data storage.
Review the IAM permissions for any role that allows for data access.
Review the Identity-Aware Proxy settings for each resource.
Create a Data Loss Prevention job.

items.question_text:
Your company has embraced a hybrid cloud strategy where some of the applications are deployed on Google Cloud. A Virtual Private Network (VPN) tunnel connects your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in Google Cloud with your company's on-premises network. Multiple applications in Google Cloud need to connect to an on-premises database server, and you want to avoid having to change the IP configuration in all of your applications when the IP of the database changes.
What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Using a Cloud DNS private zone with outbound forwarding allows applications to resolve the database by hostname rather than IP address. When the on-premises database IP changes, you only need to update the corresponding DNS record, eliminating the need to reconfigure individual application instances.
Cloud NAT (A) manages IP translation for internet egress and does not handle name resolution or internal hybrid connectivity metadata. Custom metadata (C) requires manual updates per instance, failing the requirement to avoid changing configurations.

choices.text: Configure Cloud NAT for all subnets of your VPC to be used when egressing from the VM instances.
Create a private zone on Cloud DNS, and configure the applications with the DNS name.
Configure the IP of the database as custom metadata for each instance, and query the metadata server.
Query the Compute Engine internal DNS from the applications to retrieve the IP of the database.

items.question_text: You have developed a containerized web application that will serve internal colleagues during business hours. You want to ensure that no costs are incurred outside of the hours the application is used. You have just created a new Google Cloud project and want to deploy the application. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Cloud Run (fully managed) is the correct choice because it supports scaling to zero instances when there is no traffic, ensuring no compute costs are incurred during inactive hours.
In contrast, App Engine Flexible environment requires at least one instance to be running, which incurs ongoing costs even when idle.
Cloud Run for Anthos requires an underlying GKE cluster, which also incurs persistent node costs and adds unnecessary complexity for a simple deployment on a new project.

choices.text: Deploy the container on Cloud Run for Anthos, and set the minimum number of instances to zero.
Deploy the container on Cloud Run (fully managed), and set the minimum number of instances to zero.
Deploy the container on App Engine flexible environment with autoscaling, and set the value min_instances to zero in the app.yaml.
Deploy the container on App Engine flexible environment with manual scaling, and set the value instances to zero in the app.yaml.

items.question_text: You have experimented with Google Cloud using your own credit card and expensed the costs to your company. Your company wants to streamline the billing process and charge the costs of your projects to their monthly invoice. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
The goal is to redirect charges from a personal credit card to the company's monthly invoice, which requires moving the projects to a corporate billing account.
In Google Cloud Platform, individual resources and projects are billed through their associated billing account.
To change who pays, you must reassign the project from your personal billing account to your company's billing account (Option D).
Options A, B, and C only provide visibility or minor permissions on the existing personal account but do not transfer the financial liability.

choices.text: Grant the financial team the IAM role of "Billing Account User" on the billing account linked to your credit card.
Set up BigQuery billing export and grant your financial department IAM access to query the data.
Create a ticket with Google Billing Support to ask them to send the invoice to your company.
Change the billing account of your projects to the billing account of your company.

items.question_text: You are running a data warehouse on BigQuery. A partner company is offering a recommendation engine based on the data in your data warehouse. The partner company is also running their application on Google Cloud. They manage the resources in their own project, but they need access to the BigQuery dataset in your project. You want to provide the partner company with access to the dataset. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To grant a partner company access to resources in your project, the best practice is to use a Service Account that represents their workload. The partner must create this Service Account in their own project so they retain control over its credentials and usage.
You then grant the necessary IAM roles to that external Service Account on your BigQuery dataset, allowing them to authenticate and access your data securely without sharing individual user credentials.

choices.text: Create a Service Account in your own project, and grant this Service Account access to BigQuery in your project.
Create a Service Account in your own project, and ask the partner to grant this Service Account access to BigQuery in their project.
Ask the partner to create a Service Account in their project, and have them give the Service Account access to BigQuery in their project.
Ask the partner to create a Service Account in their project, and grant their Service Account access to the BigQuery dataset in your project.
